purpose: build a model-based feature whose quality is measured, whose limits are known and whose failures are handled
entry_criteria: The problem is defined with a success measure
Data with a known source and permitted use exists
Evaluation data is held apart from training data
procedure: Start with a simple baseline, such as rules or a basic model, and record its score on the success measure.
Split the data before any tuning, keeping a test set that nobody uses for decisions until the end.
Train and compare candidates, recording data version, code version, parameters and scores for each run.
Evaluate on slices that matter, such as user groups and rare cases, not only the overall average, and examine the worst errors.
Define behavior when the model is unsure or wrong: confidence thresholds, human review and a non-model fallback.
Package the model with its version, data lineage and a monitoring plan for drift and quality after release.
deliverables: versioned model package with monitoring plan
acceptance_criteria: The model beats the baseline on the success measure
The test set was used once at the end
Slice results and worst errors are reported
A fallback exists for low confidence and failure

validation.expect: metrics per slice are printed and meet the thresholds

validation.check: check the run record contains data version, code version and parameters

failure_modes.detection: Scores too good to be true
failure_modes.response: Re-split by entity or time and rerun
Fix or limit use for that slice

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A ticket-routing model beats the keyword baseline overall, but scores lower on short messages; those below the confidence threshold go to a human queue, and weekly monitoring compares accuracy on a labelled sample.
